newsitem.title: USA: Democrat lawmakers urge end to U.S. nuke test plan.
newsitem.headline: Democrat lawmakers urge end to U.S. nuke test plan.

text.p: A group of U.S. 44 House of Representatives members urged the Clinton administration to drop plans for testing nuclear weapons without exploding them, according to a letter released on Monday.
The Energy Department is to begin within a week its first tests, called subcritical experiments, on the U.S. nuclear stockpile without exploding them.

"Mr. President, your admirable promotion of non-proliferation and your vision of a nuclear weapon-free 21st century is put at risk by a U.S. commitment to subcritical nuclear experiments," the Democratic lawmakers, backed by one Republican and one independent, said in a June 20 letter to U.S. President Bill Clinton.

"We urge you to cancel these subcritical experiments," said the letter, signed by the top Democrats on the House National Security Committee, Science Committee and Resource Committee, and House Democratic Whip David Bonior of Michigan.
The lawmakers said the U.S. programme would encourage other nations with less high-tech equipment to justify underground testing.

The Energy Department delayed its experiments to the end of June while fighting a lawsuit brought by anti-nuclear groups trying to stop the government's $40 billion programme to maintain and modernise the U.S. nuclear arsenal.
Green groups expect the judge to issue a quick ruling on whether the government may go ahead with the tests or should put them on hold pending a broader hearing of the issues.

The lawsuit said the Energy Department failed to evaluate the environmental effects of its programme and failed to explore alternatives to its costly plan to keep weapons ready for use without violating international test bans.
